skill.name: data-storytelling

content.value_statement: Raw metrics often fail to guide stakeholder decisions. This skill turns analysis into clear narratives, visual structures, and action plans.
actual_capabilities: Explains story structures for analytics presentations.
Provides problem-solution, trend, and comparison frameworks.
Suggests progressive reveal, contrast, annotation, and highlighting techniques.
Offers slide, dashboard, and executive summary templates.
Gives writing patterns for headlines, transitions, uncertainty, and calls to action.
limitations: Does not calculate metrics or verify source data.
Does not create finished charts without a separate visualization workflow.
Requires audience goals, business context, and available data from the user.
Examples use sample business scenarios and need adaptation before use.

use_cases.title: Prepare Executive Reporting
use_cases.description: Turn quarterly metrics into a concise story with insight, context, recommendation, and decision request.

use_cases.title: Shape Investor Updates
use_cases.description: Convert growth metrics and risks into a persuasive narrative for funding or board discussions.

use_cases.title: Explain Product Performance
use_cases.description: Present adoption, retention, and funnel changes as a clear product decision story.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Simple Data Story
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for turning a metric summary into a basic narrative.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short story with setup, conflict, resolution, and one recommendation. Audience: [audience]. Data summary: [paste summary].

prompt_templates.title: Turn Metrics Into Slides
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for planning a presentation flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seven-slide data story for [business topic]. Include headline, context, discovery, deep dive, recommendation, impact, and decision needed.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Strategic Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for choosing between two business paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for [audience]. Include criteria, tradeoffs, risks, and a final recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Executive Narrative
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for refining a full stakeholder presentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my analysis and create an executive-ready narrative. Include hook, key insight, visual sequence, uncertainty statement, decision request, and next actions.

output_examples.input: A churn analysis shows early disengagement, low feature adoption, and a high first-quarter cancellation rate.
output_examples.output: Headline: Preventable onboarding gaps are driving churn. The story links weak early engagement to lost revenue and recommends a 14-day activation program.

output_examples.input: A quarterly review shows revenue growth, higher acquisition cost, and lower trial conversion.
output: Start with revenue growth as the hook.
Show acquisition cost as the tension.
Recommend reallocating spend and testing a shorter onboarding path.

output_examples.input: A market expansion analysis compares EMEA and APAC across growth, complexity, competition, and readiness.
output_examples.output: The narrative frames the decision as growth versus complexity. It recommends the region with stronger opportunity and clearer launch steps.

best_practices: Lead with the business insight before the supporting metrics.
Choose visuals that reveal one decision-relevant pattern at a time.
State confidence, limits, and assumptions before asking for action.
anti_patterns: Do not paste every metric into a presentation without a narrative.
Do not start with methodology when the audience needs a decision.
Do not use jargon that obscures the insight for non-technical stakeholders.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create data narratives, executive summaries, dashboard stories, and presentation flows for stakeholder decisions.

faq.question: Can it build charts directly?
faq.answer: It gives chart guidance and example structures, but it does not render final visuals by itself.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for analysts, product managers, founders, and leaders who need to explain data clearly.

faq.question: Does it verify my data?
faq.answer: No. Users must validate source data, calculations, assumptions, and statistical claims before presenting.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, decision goal, key metrics, business context, constraints, and any known caveats.
